text:
evan: Heads up, we've got a spike of 502s from edge-lb -> gpu-pool in us-west2, started ~09:12 UTC. models failing to fetch context, clients see timeouts.

karen: +1 seeing same from monitoring. Health checks flapping, target group marking nodes unhealthy. :alarm_clock:

linh: Looking at node logs, I see a ton of `ECONNRESET` to NAT gateway IPs. Suspect conntrack exhaustion on the NAT side. Pulling conntrack counts now.

linh: `sudo conntrack -S | grep entries` -> `entries 65536` and `max 65536` (NAT instance appears saturated).

ryan: That explains intermittent TCP resets. Are we on NAT gateway or NAT instance for that subnet?

evan: It's a NAT instance in the older edge VPC (we never migrated that AZ). Ops console shows CPU low but tcp connection table is pegged.

karen: How are ELB healthchecks coming from (IPs)? Could be many source IPs causing ephemeral port explosion.

linh: VPC Flow Logs snippet for one node:
```
07:09:22 ACCEPT tcp 10.10.44.72:32768 52.93.10.5:443  ESTABLISHED
07:09:22 ACCEPT tcp 10.10.44.72:32769 54.230.0.12:443 ESTABLISHED
... (thousands) ...
```
Multiple distinct destination IPs (external model retrievals + telemetry), ports all high ephemeral range.

ryan: Ops-bot reported a deploy at 09:05 that increased outbound rate (model cache prefetcher). Might have created many short-lived outbound connections.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0423 - NAT conntrack saturation causing LB healthcheck failures (assigned: linh)

evan: Workarounds: 1) change nodes to use private NAT gateway with higher conntrack, 2) enable connection tracking helpers? 3) reduce prefetch concurrency. Quickest: reduce prefetcher to 20 threads.

karen: Can we also add iptables rule to time out ESTABLISHED faster? Current `nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established` default 432000s — way too long for short connections.

linh: On a test node I lowered to 300s and freed ~12k entries within a minute. Command: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=300`

ryan: Do we need to roll that cluster-wide? Risk: may affect long-lived streams (video use) but our gpu-model-serving is short-lived per request.

evan: Plan: (1) throttle prefetcher immed (rollback deploy), (2) apply temporary sysctl via DaemonSet to gpu node pool to reduce established timeout, (3) open ticket to migrate subnet to managed NAT gateway (higher conntrack capacity) and consider SNAT pools.

karen: I'm on it — throttling prefetcher now. Patch rolling back 5 pods. :white_check_mark:

linh: Deploying DaemonSet with sysctl change (testing on one node first). Will monitor conntrack and LB target health.

evan: Thanks. Post back numbers once conntrack drops and healthchecks recover.

linh: Quick numbers after throttling + sysctl on one node:
```
before: entries=65534/65536, failed_conn=3487
after: entries=51220/65536, failed_conn=122
ALB healthy targets: 2/3 -> 3/3 after ~90s
```

ryan: Nice. Next steps: schedule NAT gateway migration w/ infra team, add alert on conntrack usage > 70% for that subnet's NAT, and add guidance in runbook.

evan: I'll create follow-up RFC for NAT migration and runbook updates. Great catch y'all. :clap:
